# Getting Started

## Provider configuration

Requirements: Terraform >= 1.11.0 and < 2.0.0, an accessible OnPager Control API,
and a bearer token with the permissions required by the configuration.

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.0, < 2.0.0"

  required_providers {
    onpager = {
      source = "onpager/onpager"
    }
  }
}

# Supply values through variables or use the ONPAGER_* environment fallback.
provider "onpager" {
  endpoint = var.onpager_endpoint
  token    = var.onpager_token
  timezone = var.onpager_timezone
}

variable "onpager_endpoint" {
  description = "Control base URL. Null uses ONPAGER_ENDPOINT."
  type        = string
  default     = null
}

variable "onpager_token" {
  description = "Control bearer token. Null uses ONPAGER_TOKEN."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  default     = null
}

variable "onpager_timezone" {
  description = "Optional IANA request timezone. Null sends no override."
  type        = string
  default     = null
}
```

Set the input variables or use `ONPAGER_ENDPOINT` and `ONPAGER_TOKEN`. For Vault
integration and native grants, see [authentication](authentication.md).

Provider installation through `terraform init` requires a published release.
For a local build, use `task dev` and its development override as documented in the
[contributor guide](https://github.com/onpager/terraform-provider-onpager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Team and service configuration

This configuration owns a team, a service and one explicit membership. The user
already exists and is selected by local credential login.

```terraform
resource "onpager_team" "operations" {
  name = "Operations"
}

resource "onpager_service" "api" {
  name    = "API"
  team_id = onpager_team.operations.id
}

data "onpager_user" "operator" {
  local_login = "operator"
}

resource "onpager_team_membership" "operator" {
  team_id = onpager_team.operations.id
  user_id = data.onpager_user.operator.id
}
```

For an OIDC user, select by UUID or exact email. `local_login` refers only to a
local credential. Data sources do not assume ownership of the selected objects.
Email and group-name selectors reject ambiguous matches; name selectors are exact
and case-sensitive. Role/group keys are stable tenant identifiers.

## Notification connections

Configure shared transports with [bots](../resources/bot.md),
[voice providers](../resources/voice_provider.md) and
[outgoing webhooks](../resources/outgoing_webhook.md). Bot and voice UUIDs are
also their managed delivery-channel UUIDs. Use explicit channel and destination
UUIDs for catalog bindings. Terraform does not discover destinations or enroll
personal contacts.

Use `enabled = false` to stage a connection before runtime activation. Disabled
creation still requires valid public settings and all required credentials.
Template overrides select their own explicit `delivery_provider` and `language`;
they do not configure a user's language preference or send a notification.

## Composed configuration

The [team configuration example](https://github.com/onpager/terraform-provider-onpager/tree/main/examples/team-configuration)
includes routing filters, an integration, a calendar, a schedule with primary
rotation, an escalation chain, and explicit IAM definitions and assignments.
It uses the standard Terraform root configuration layout:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `terraform.tf` | Terraform and provider requirements |
| `providers.tf` | Provider configuration |
| `variables.tf` | Typed input variables |
| `main.tf` | Resources |
| `outputs.tf` | Output values |

Required inputs are `team_name`, `service_name`, `operator_user_id`,
`rotation_starts_at` and `iam_key_prefix`. The example README defines optional
OIDC mapping, template override, delivery target, request timezone and temporary
schedule override inputs. Existing user/channel/target prerequisites are explicit.

## Apply and state

From the configuration directory:

```shell
terraform init
terraform validate
terraform plan -out=tfplan
terraform apply tfplan
```

An integration's webhook URL and token configure the source system separately.
The token is sensitive and stored in Terraform state. Review the
[lifecycle guide](lifecycle.md) before import or destroy, and the
[suppression/enrichment guide](suppression-enrichment.md) before assigning
whole-tenant configuration ownership.
